title: A lane session's title opens with "Lane <branch slug>:"
why: Lane sessions in the owner's sidebar have free titles in some repos, so he cannot tell which branch a lane runs.
source: Retrospective 21:18 CST Nov 11, from the owner's 21:17 CST sidebar screenshot
note: Seen: degen's local lanes read "Lane small-screen-fixes: 519, 520"; home's read "Thermostat fan settings (Resideo)", with no slug. Both run the same claude-settings. On main 2684959d6 no rule, template or guard sets a lane session's title; guard.py:1880 only refuses a session-number lane name, and rule git-slug-then-claim-number says to name a lane by its branch slug. Ask: (1) the lane start text in skill project-ops gives one title form, "Lane <branch slug>: <task>"; (2) the guard refuses a lane start (mcp__ccd_session__start_session, or create_session with tag cs-build:lane) whose title does not open with "Lane <slug>:". Proof: a red test on today's code with a free-titled lane start; a titled one passes. Changes a guard's verdict: a lane with full review. Code, not prose. Waits for the fan-out (owner 13:51).
